title: What Is ARTAK? The Augmented Reality Team Awareness Kit, Explained
excerpt: ARTAK is Eolian's patented mixed-reality command-and-control platform: a 3D common operating picture that runs on headsets, tablets, and laptops, works air-gapped at the edge, and federates with the TAK ecosystem. Here's what it is, who uses it, and how to buy it.

children.text: Ask ten people in the defense technology community what ARTAK is and you will get ten different answers: a headset thing, a TAK plugin, a training simulator, a mapping tool. None of those are right, and the confusion costs real programs real time.
So here is the direct answer, and then the detail behind it.

ARTAK, the Augmented Reality Team Awareness Kit, is EolianVR's patented command-and-control platform that renders a live, shared, three-dimensional operating picture across mixed-reality headsets, tablets, phones, and laptops.

It is used for mission planning, rehearsal, and real-time situational awareness. It runs at the edge without a network, federates with the TAK family and other C2 systems, and has been fielded across most components of U.S. Special Operations Command since 2022.
The rest of this page answers the questions we actually get asked, by operators, by program managers, and by the contracting officers who have to write the order.
The problem ARTAK solves

Every staff section plans in a flat world. Maps, imagery, slide decks, and a taped-off rock drill on a motor pool floor. Then the force steps into terrain that is three-dimensional, vertical, subterranean, and interior, and the plan has to be re-derived on the fly by whoever happens to be standing there.

ARTAK collapses that gap. The planning environment is the terrain: accurate 3D geometry with building interiors, multi-floor structures, and subterranean networks, shared simultaneously across every participant's device. A squad leader in a headset, a fires planner on a laptop, and a coalition liaison on a tablet all manipulate the same objects in the same space. When the plan changes, it changes for everyone at once.
That is the difference between a visualization tool and a command-and-control platform. ARTAK is the second one.
How ARTAK fits the TAK ecosystem
ARTAK is not a competitor to ATAK, WinTAK, or iTAK. It is the three-dimensional, multi-user layer above them.

The TAK family solved the two-dimensional shared map on the device an operator already carries. ARTAK federates with TAK Server and the broader TAK ecosystem and extends the same picture into volumetric space, where terrain masking, weapons envelopes, building interiors, and vertical maneuver actually live. Units keep the TAK infrastructure they have already accredited, trained on, and budgeted for. ARTAK plugs into it.

The same is true beyond TAK. ARTAK federates today with Anduril's Lattice, ArduPilot, and ADS-B, and ingests live JADC2 data streams. Data comes in through a low-code Python SDK or a no-code UI, so a mission systems team can wire a new sensor or feed without a software release from us.
The architecture underneath
ARTAK is built on the Eolian Simulation Platform (ESP), protected by U.S. Patent 11,297,164 B2 and International Patent WO 2019/217437 A2.

ESP is a Modular Open System Architecture design, per the MOSA mandate at 10 U.S.C. 4401: containerized microservices orchestrated on Kubernetes and MicroK8s, with container images signed and scanned using Trivy and Cosign, and approved containers available through Iron Bank and Platform One. It has been tested across edge, on-premises, and DoD cloud environments, with an IL-5 path in progress.

Two consequences matter commercially. First, modules can be upgraded, replaced, or competed independently; you are not buying a monolith that has to be re-procured whole. Second, the Image Generation Service performs distributed server-side rendering and streams media to clients inside and outside the system boundary, which is how ARTAK puts a high-fidelity 3D picture in front of a user whose device could never render it locally.
Where ARTAK is fielded

ARTAK has been fielded across most components of USSOCOM since 2022 and has supported U.S. Army, U.S. Marine Corps, NATO SOF, and partner-force users. Eolian has attracted roughly $18M in total Department of Defense funding to date, including a USSOCOM prototype OTA and a Defense Innovation Unit 5G Expeditionary Advanced Base Operations effort.
That matters for one reason: ARTAK is not a prototype looking for a first user. It is a fielded capability looking for its next one.
What changed in Block 3
Block 1 put a high-quality 3D map in an operator's hands at the edge. Block 2 let units build those maps themselves, without a network.
Block 3 turns the map into a staff planning environment.
The headline feature is the Weapon Inventory: 200+ U.S. weapon systems, each carrying its real range, engagement envelope, and blast radius, and enforced.
You cannot drag a weapon farther than it can actually shoot.
Coverage gaps show up as gaps, and a fires plan that does not close is obvious to everyone standing in the terrain before it is ever briefed.

Block 3 also adds thousands of icons, nodes, symbols, maneuvers, and control measures built to MIL-STD-2525E; render-through so graphics never disappear behind a ridgeline; an improved Immersion Mode for eye-level walkthroughs of interiors and subterranean spaces; six new base maps; and multi-user HMD synchronization so every headset in the room holds the same picture at the same moment.
Buying it

ARTAK is available as a software license on hardware you already own, as an enterprise subscription, or as a pre-configured kit. Eolian is registered in SAM.gov (UEI HHN2E2LNBSV5, CAGE 7RLL6) as a small business, and has delivered under SBIR, OTA, and direct award. Most single-unit kit purchases fall under the simplified acquisition threshold, which is why a unit with available O&M funds can often move in weeks rather than quarters.
The Common Questions below cover the specifics: contents, cost, funding, and the actual step-by-step.

faqs.question: What is ARTAK?
faqs.answer: ARTAK is EolianVR's patented command-and-control platform that renders a live, shared 3D operating picture across mixed-reality headsets, tablets, phones, and laptops. Teams use it for mission planning, rehearsal, and real-time situational awareness. ARTAK runs at the edge without a network connection, federates with the TAK ecosystem and other C2 systems, and has been fielded across most components of U.S. Special Operations Command since 2022.

faqs.question: What does ARTAK stand for?
faqs.answer: ARTAK stands for Augmented Reality Team Awareness Kit. The name signals its relationship to the TAK (Team Awareness Kit) family of situational-awareness tools used across the Department of Defense. ARTAK extends that shared-picture concept into three dimensions and mixed reality.

faqs.question: How is ARTAK different from ATAK, WinTAK, and iTAK?
faqs.answer: ATAK, WinTAK, and iTAK deliver a shared two-dimensional map on a phone, tablet, or Windows machine. ARTAK is the three-dimensional, multi-user layer above them. ARTAK federates with TAK Server rather than replacing it, so units keep the TAK infrastructure they have already accredited and trained on. ARTAK adds value on volumetric problems a 2D map cannot represent: terrain masking, weapons envelopes, building interiors, multi-floor structures, subterranean networks, and vertical maneuver.

faqs.question: What hardware does ARTAK run on?
faqs.answer: ARTAK is device-agnostic. ARTAK runs on mixed-reality headsets, Android and iOS tablets and phones, laptops, and desktop PCs, and users on different device classes can share the same session simultaneously. Because the Image Generation Service performs server-side rendering and streams the result to the client, ARTAK can present a high-fidelity 3D picture on devices that could not render it locally. Units can deploy ARTAK on hardware they already own or purchase a pre-configured Eolian kit.

faqs.question: Does ARTAK work without a network connection?
faqs.answer: Yes. ARTAK runs fully air-gapped at the tactical edge on a local edge server, with no reliance on a reach-back connection or cloud service. Adaptive level-of-detail and dynamic rendering profiles let ARTAK continue operating in DDIL conditions: degraded, denied, intermittent, and limited-bandwidth environments. Beginning with Block 2, units can also generate their own 3D maps locally rather than waiting on a networked mapping pipeline.

faqs.question: What systems does ARTAK integrate with?
faqs.answer: ARTAK federates today with the TAK family (TAK Server, ATAK, WinTAK, iTAK), Anduril's Lattice, ArduPilot, and ADS-B, and ingests live JADC2 data streams. New data sources can be added through a low-code Python SDK or a no-code configuration UI, so a mission systems team can connect a sensor or feed without waiting on a vendor software release. ARTAK's underlying architecture is MOSA-compliant per 10 U.S.C. 4401 and built on open standards including REST APIs, TAK protocols, and OGC standards.

faqs.question: Who uses ARTAK today?
faqs.answer: ARTAK has been fielded across most components of U.S. Special Operations Command since 2022, and has supported U.S. Army, U.S. Marine Corps, NATO SOF, and partner-force users. Eolian has attracted approximately $18M in total Department of Defense funding, including a USSOCOM prototype Other Transaction Agreement and a Defense Innovation Unit 5G Expeditionary Advanced Base Operations effort.

faqs.question: What is included in the ARTAK Squad Kit?
faqs.answer: The ARTAK Squad Kit includes eight mixed-reality headsets, one Samsung tablet, one WiFi/LTE network node, one edge server, and a one-year software subscription. It ships as a self-contained package that gives a squad a live 3D view of the operating environment and integrates with ATAK and JADC2 data. Other configurations are available, including larger command-post kits, custom builds, and software-only licenses installed on hardware a unit already owns.

faqs.question: How much does ARTAK cost?
faqs.answer: The ARTAK Squad Kit, which includes eight XR headsets, a tablet, a network node, an edge server, and a one-year software subscription, is priced at $234,683 as of 31 July 2026. That places a single kit below the $350,000 simplified acquisition threshold, which is why many units can buy one without a full competitive acquisition. Software-only licenses, enterprise subscriptions, and multi-kit or custom configurations are priced separately. Contact mike@eolianvr.com for a current quote.

faqs.question: How does a military unit buy ARTAK?
faqs.answer: Most units buy a single ARTAK kit through simplified acquisition procedures. The sequence is: write a one- or two-sentence statement of need; confirm with your S-4 or comptroller that O&M funds are available and appropriate, and obtain the funding citation; choose a payment method, either a Government Purchase Card at or below the micro-purchase threshold or a purchase order above it; submit a purchase request with the item description, cost, funding citation, and payment method; your contracting officer checks mandatory sources, documents price reasonableness, verifies EolianVR's SAM.gov registration, and issues the order; the unit receives and inspects the kit. EolianVR is registered in SAM.gov as a small business under UEI HHN2E2LNBSV5 and CAGE 7RLL6. Confirm all thresholds and funding determinations with your contracting officer, comptroller, and counsel.

faqs.question: What is ARTAK's security and accreditation posture?
faqs.answer: ARTAK is built on a containerized microservices architecture running on Kubernetes and MicroK8s, with container images signed and scanned using Cosign and Trivy and approved containers available through Iron Bank and Platform One. ARTAK has been tested across edge, on-premises, and DoD cloud environments, with an IL-5 path in progress. ARTAK operates today under existing Department of Defense authorizations within USSOCOM enclaves, with RMF-aligned controls already in production. Accreditation is inherited from the hosting enclave rather than carried independently, so the path for a new customer runs through their own authorizing official, a process Eolian has supported repeatedly.

faqs.question: What is new in ARTAK Block 3?
faqs.answer: Block 3 turns ARTAK from a 3D map into a full staff planning environment. Its central feature is the Weapon Inventory: 200+ U.S. weapon systems carrying real range, engagement envelope, and blast radius data, enforced in the interface so a weapon cannot be placed beyond its actual range. Block 3 also adds thousands of icons, nodes, symbols, maneuvers, and control measures built to MIL-STD-2525E with emphasis on higher-echelon graphics; render-through so symbols stay visible behind buildings and terrain; an improved Immersion Mode for eye-level walkthroughs of interiors and subterranean spaces; six new base maps; multi-user HMD synchronization; and search and filter by warfighting function.

title: Who Is EolianVR? The Defense Technology Company Behind ARTAK
excerpt: EolianVR is a small-business defense technology company and systems integrator building mixed-reality command-and-control software for multi-domain operations. Founded in 2016, fielded with USSOCOM, and structured so government customers can actually buy from us.

children.text: Most defense technology companies are one of two things. Either a large integrator with the contract vehicles and the compliance staff but a decade-long delivery cycle, or a fast startup with a compelling demo and no idea how a contracting officer actually writes an order.
EolianVR is deliberately neither.
EolianVR, Inc. is a small-business defense technology company and systems integrator that builds mixed-reality command-and-control software for multi-domain operations.

Founded in 2016 and headquartered in Largo, Florida, Eolian's flagship platform, ARTAK (the Augmented Reality Team Awareness Kit), has been fielded across U.S. Special Operations Command and deployed on six continents.
This page answers the questions we get from program managers, contracting officers, partners, and investors trying to figure out who we are and whether we are a real option.
What we build
Three products, one architecture.
ARTAK

is the flagship: a patented, device-agnostic platform that turns mission planning from a PowerPoint-and-sand-table exercise into a live digital twin of the battlespace. Commanders, staff, and operators plan, brief, rehearse, and command inside the same 3D environment, from headsets, tablets, laptops, or PCs, together, in real time.
Read the full ARTAK explainer
Map Maker

is the companion that feeds it. Raw drone imagery or LiDAR goes in; a high-quality 3D map comes out in minutes, fully automated, with no internet connection required. Output is non-proprietary and works with ARTAK, ATAK, WinTAK, and other government systems. A team can fly a small UAS, process the imagery on a laptop in their barracks, and rehearse on the resulting digital twin the same day.
STAK
, the Space Team Awareness Kit, extends the same architecture into the space domain: 3D visualization of satellite constellations, orbital dynamics, and space domain operations.
All three are implementations of the Eolian Mixed Reality Platform, protected by U.S. Patent 11,297,164 B2 and International Patent WO 2019/217437 A2.
Why we exist
The Global War on Terror ended. Great Power Competition did not wait.

Today's operations span mega-cities, subterranean tunnel networks, maritime and undersea environments, cyberspace, and orbit. The planning tools most units still rely on, flat maps and static slides and disconnected feeds, were designed for a different problem. They force every commander to reassemble a three-dimensional world in their head, individually, from two-dimensional inputs, and then hope everyone assembled the same one.

Eolian builds the tools that close that gap. Our mission is straightforward: give the world's most capable forces the command-and-control and situational-awareness tools that turn information advantage into decisive action.
How we're built to be bought from
Good technology that cannot be procured is not a capability. Eolian is structured, registered, and experienced so that a program office can move.

We are an Other Small Business, 100% U.S.-owned, registered in SAM.gov under CAGE code 7RLL6 and UEI HHN2E2LNBSV5, with 541511 (Custom Computer Programming Services) as our primary NAICS. We qualify as a nontraditional defense contractor, which is what makes Other Transaction Agreements a practical path rather than a theoretical one.

We have delivered under prototype OTAs, a production OTA, congressional appropriations, and direct award, and we hold teaming partnerships with Booz Allen Hamilton and MITRE. Single-kit purchases typically fall under the simplified acquisition threshold, which is why a unit with available O&M funds can often move in weeks rather than quarters.

To be direct about what we are not: Eolian does not hold SDVOSB, 8(a), WOSB, or HUBZone status. If your acquisition strategy depends on one of those set-asides, we are not the right prime, but we are frequently the right teammate.
The proof

In November 2022, Eolian was selected as one of ten companies in the first cohort of the Accelerate the Procurement and Fielding of Innovative Technologies (APFIT) program, a congressionally funded effort to move proven capability out of the prototype valley of death. Nominated by USSOCOM, the award was a $10M three-year Production OTA covering ARTAK kits and software licenses for USSOCOM units. Eolian transitioned from a 2020 Prototype OTA directly to Production, which is uncommon.

Independent evaluation backs it up. At the Army Expeditionary Warrior Experiment 2024, a force-on-force assessment run by the U.S. Army Maneuver Battle Lab with U.S., British, and German soldiers, 93% of participating soldiers rated ARTAK effective to very effective for mission planning, 86% for briefing, and 77% for situational awareness. 100% agreed it increased command-and-control capability.
Eolian has also been recognized with the U.S. Department of Labor's HIRE Vets Gold Medallion Award three years running (2022 through 2024) and Unity's 2022 Creator Award for Government & Aerospace.
Beyond the Department of Defense
The same architecture that lets a Special Forces team rehearse a hard-target defeat lets an emergency manager coordinate a wildfire response, or a security operations center run a major public event.

Eolian works with Five Eyes and NATO partner forces, including demonstrations at multinational exercises such as Project Convergence Capstone 5, and has engaged customers across disaster response, emergency management, law enforcement, border security, academic research, and commercial industry. Dual-use is not a pivot for us; it is the same product meeting an adjacent need.

faqs.question: What is EolianVR?
faqs.answer: EolianVR, Inc. is a defense technology company and systems integrator that builds mixed-reality command-and-control and mission-planning software for multi-domain operations. Founded in 2016 and headquartered in Largo, Florida, EolianVR develops the Augmented Reality Team Awareness Kit (ARTAK), a patented 3D command-and-control platform fielded across U.S. Special Operations Command and deployed on six continents. EolianVR is an Other Small Business, 100% U.S.-owned, and registered in SAM.gov.

faqs.question: What products does EolianVR build?
faqs.answer: EolianVR builds three products on a shared, patented architecture. ARTAK (Augmented Reality Team Awareness Kit) is a device-agnostic 3D command-and-control and mission-planning platform. Map Maker generates high-quality 3D maps in minutes from raw drone imagery or LiDAR, fully automated and without an internet connection, outputting non-proprietary formats compatible with ARTAK, ATAK, WinTAK, and other government systems. STAK (Space Team Awareness Kit) extends the architecture to space domain awareness, including satellite constellations and orbital dynamics. EolianVR also delivers custom AR/VR/MR development and systems integration services.

faqs.question: When was EolianVR founded, and who leads it?
faqs.answer: EolianVR was founded in 2016 by Michael McCormack and Mike Simmons. McCormack serves as CEO and designed and built the core ARTAK platform; his background spans software development and military technology focused on near-peer adversary challenges, mixed reality, and situational awareness. Simmons serves as COO and brings 15+ years launching and scaling companies across multiple industries, with a BBA in Finance and Marketing from the University of Miami.

faqs.question: Where is EolianVR located?
faqs.answer: EolianVR is headquartered in Largo, Florida, in the Tampa Bay region, placing the company in the same area as U.S. Special Operations Command and U.S. Central Command at MacDill Air Force Base. EolianVR supports customers and exercises across the United States and internationally, and ARTAK is deployed on six continents.

faqs.question: Is EolianVR a small business? What socioeconomic designations does it hold?
faqs.answer: Yes. EolianVR qualifies as an Other Small Business under NAICS 541511 and is 100% U.S.-owned. EolianVR does not hold SDVOSB, 8(a), WOSB, or HUBZone status, and does not claim eligibility for those set-asides. Program offices with small-business goals can credit an award to EolianVR against small-business targets; acquisitions requiring a specific socioeconomic set-aside are better served by teaming, which EolianVR does regularly with both large integrators and other small businesses.

faqs.question: Is EolianVR a nontraditional defense contractor?
faqs.answer: Yes. EolianVR qualifies as a nontraditional defense contractor as that term is defined in 10 U.S.C. 3014: an entity not currently performing, and not having performed for at least the preceding one-year period, a Department of Defense contract subject to full Cost Accounting Standards coverage. This matters for acquisition strategy. Under 10 U.S.C. 4022, significant participation by a nontraditional defense contractor is one of the conditions that allows an agency to award an Other Transaction Agreement for a prototype project without a one-third cost-share requirement. EolianVR has delivered under prototype and production OTAs on that basis.

faqs.question: What contract vehicles has EolianVR delivered under?
faqs.answer: EolianVR has delivered under Other Transaction Agreements for both prototype and production, congressional appropriations, and direct award, and holds an Information Exchange Agreement with Washington Headquarters Services on behalf of the Assistant Secretary of Defense for Mission Capabilities. Specific past performance includes a 2020 USSOCOM Prototype OTA, a Defense Innovation Unit 5G Expeditionary Advanced Base Operations Prototype OTA (HQ0845-23-9-0046), and a USSOCOM-nominated APFIT Production OTA awarded in November 2022. EolianVR is registered in SAM.gov, holds teaming partnerships with Booz Allen Hamilton and MITRE, and also teams as a subcontractor where that is the better path.

faqs.question: Who are EolianVR's customers?
faqs.answer: EolianVR's primary customer is U.S. Special Operations Command, where ARTAK has been fielded across most components since 2022. Other users and customers include the U.S. Army and USASOC, the U.S. Marine Corps and MARSOC, the U.S. Air Force, the Department of Homeland Security, the Defense Innovation Unit, ERDCWERX, and NATO SOF and partner forces. EolianVR also works with allied ministries of defence, national laboratories, academic institutions, and commercial defense manufacturers; those relationships are named individually only where the customer has approved public reference.

faqs.question: What is APFIT, and what did EolianVR win?
faqs.answer: APFIT, or Accelerate the Procurement and Fielding of Innovative Technologies, is a congressionally funded Department of Defense program created to move proven prototypes into production and fielding rather than letting them stall after a successful demonstration. In November 2022, EolianVR was selected as one of ten companies in APFIT's first cohort, nominated by U.S. Special Operations Command, and awarded a $10M three-year Production Other Transaction Agreement covering ARTAK kits and software licenses for USSOCOM units. EolianVR transitioned directly from a 2020 Prototype OTA to Production, which is an uncommon outcome in defense acquisition.

faqs.question: Has EolianVR's technology been independently evaluated?
faqs.answer: Yes. At the Army Expeditionary Warrior Experiment (AEWE) 2024, a force-on-force technology assessment run by the U.S. Army Maneuver Battle Lab with U.S. Army, British Army, and German soldiers, 93% of participating soldiers rated ARTAK effective to very effective for mission planning, 86% for briefing, and 77% for situational awareness, and 100% agreed it increased command-and-control capability. ARTAK has additionally been assessed through Defense Innovation Unit prototype evaluation, USSOCOM technology events, and allied multinational exercises including Project Convergence Capstone 5.

Its primary NAICS code is 541511 (Custom Computer Programming Services), with additional codes including 541512, 541519, 423420, 423430, 423490, 541613, and 611430. Business type is Other Small Business, 100% U.S.-owned, founded in 2016. For a current capability statement or to request quoting and vehicle information, contact mike@eolianvr.com.

faqs.question: Does EolianVR work outside the U.S. defense market?
faqs.answer: Yes. EolianVR supports Five Eyes and NATO partner forces, including demonstrations at multinational exercises such as Project Convergence Capstone 5. Beyond defense, the same platform applies to disaster response, emergency management, security command and control, law enforcement, fire and rescue, border security, and space operations. International engagements are subject to applicable U.S. export control requirements.

faqs.answer: The fastest path is a live demonstration using your own area of operations, available in person or remotely. Email mike@eolianvr.com to schedule one, request a current capability statement, or discuss a specific requirement, teaming arrangement, or contract vehicle.
